title: Synthetic and fictional data
content: The platform uses fictional machines and synthetic telemetry for a local portfolio project. It must not be treated as real industrial equipment state or official manufacturer data.

title: Bronze Silver Gold architecture
content: Telemetry flows through local Kafka into Spark Bronze Parquet, then deterministic Silver validation and deduplication, then Gold descriptive analytics. PostgreSQL stores curated operational records, not raw high-volume telemetry.

title: Materialized read API
content: FastAPI serves already-materialized PostgreSQL state. API requests do not run Spark, Kafka, model inference, SHAP generation, anomaly scoring, or drift calculation.

title: AI4I failure probability
content: failure_probability is the frozen AI4I model output for predicted failure risk. It is a model estimate, not an observed failure, and failure_prediction is a model decision using the frozen 0.14 threshold.

title: Frozen AI4I threshold
content: The AI4I classifier uses a frozen decision threshold of 0.14. The threshold is part of the retained model policy and is not changed by the API, dashboard, alerts, or copilot.

title: Anomaly score
content: anomaly_score is an Isolation Forest detector score where higher values are more anomalous. It is not a probability, and anomaly_flag is a detector decision, not a confirmed equipment failure.

title: PSI drift monitoring
content: PSI is a population stability index diagnostic for input distribution shift. PSI drift is not model accuracy, not model performance, and not automatic evidence that retraining is required.

title: SHAP model attribution
content: SHAP values describe how model inputs contributed to one positive-class model output. Positive values push the model output toward higher predicted failure risk and negative values push it lower. SHAP is not causality or physical root-cause analysis.

title: Operational alerts
content: Alerts are deterministic monitoring records derived from persisted prediction and anomaly rows. They are not confirmed failures and the local copilot cannot acknowledge, resolve, create, or delete alerts.

title: Local copilot limitations
content: The copilot runs locally with Ollama and uses read-only tools plus trusted knowledge retrieval. Natural-language responses can still make mistakes, so structured tool results are the authoritative platform evidence.
